title: Nutritious Nourishing Korean Pork Doenjang Jjigae
description: A traditional Korean fermented soybean paste stew made with tandoor-cooked pork, tamarind pulp, and a variety of vegetables, served in a warm ceramic tagine.
instructions: Heat the tandoor-cooked pork fat in a large ceramic tagine over medium heat.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the zucchini and carrots and cook until tender, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the gochujang and doenjang and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the pork shoulder and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add the tamarind pulp, Korean chili flakes, and salt, and stir to combine.
Bring the stew to a simmer and cook for 10-15 minutes, or until the pork is tender.
Stir in the green onions and cook for an additional 1-2 minutes.
Serve the stew hot, garnished with additional green onions if desired.
Note: If using a slow cooker, cook on low for 6-8 hours or on high for 3-4 hours.
Serve with steamed rice or noodles, if desired.
Cook pork to an internal temperature of 63°C / 145°F and let it rest for 3 minutes before serving.
